title: Hyper-V Host Network Interface Discard or Error Counter Increase
exclusions: Measures five-minute increases in four documented Windows `Network Interface` raw packet counters on exact inventoried Hyper-V host interfaces: `Packets Received Discarded`, `Packets Received Errors`, `Packets Outbound Discarded`, and `Packets Outbound Errors`. It does not claim nonexistent `Hyper-V Virtual Network Adapter` dropped-packet counters, does not observe every Hyper-V extensible-switch port or guest vNIC, and cannot identify whether the physical NIC, host vEthernet interface, virtual switch policy/extension, driver, firmware, physical switch, cable, guest, or remote path caused a packet loss. A row is a positive packet-count delta, not a rate, percentage, sustained outage, or proof of application impact. Counter reset/wrap, missing/duplicate/late samples, instance rename, and mapping drift are source-health findings. SR-IOV traffic may bypass parts of the software path. The local source type, five-minute window, any-increase threshold, inventory, and exceptions are deployment policy. This UC changes no adapter, switch, QoS, VMQ, RSS/vRSS, SR-IOV, VLAN, driver, or firmware setting.
evidence: After deployment, retain `hyperv_host_interface_discard_or_error_increase`, ACL, five-minute schedule, dispatch rows, alerts, and throttle state; effective `[perfmon://HyperVHostNetworkInterface]` input and assignment; raw 60-second events with exact object/counter/instance, packet-count Value, host, event/index time, and source type; host/instance-to-adapter-ID/switch inventory and exception revisions; sample-gap, reset/wrap, duplicate, invalid-value, and unmapped-interface controls; fixed delta/boundary outputs; current Performance Monitor and `Get-NetAdapterStatistics` readings; `Get-VMSwitch` and `Get-VMNetworkAdapter -All` topology; physical-switch/NIC driver/firmware, VMQ/RSS/vRSS/SR-IOV, QoS/ACL/extension, host/guest workload, packet-capture, and service evidence used in diagnosis; incident/change disposition; and later clean deltas plus service validation. These artifacts show Windows interface counter increases, not complete virtual-switch loss attribution. This documentation-only review collected no counter, ran no search, changed no network, and produced no alert or production evidence.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Fix dispatch at 2026-07-29T06:10:00Z. In an isolated index, ingest `Network Interface` / `Packets Received Discarded` samples for `host=hv-lab-01`, `instance=Ethernet 2` at 06:04 through 06:09 with cumulative Values 100,100,101,101,104,104. Add one active exact inventory row with immutable adapter ID and no exception. Expect exactly one 06:05–06:10 row with `sample_count=5`, `valid_delta_count=5`, `packet_increment=4`, `finding=received_discard_increase`, `unit=packets`, and no reset.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Run isolated variants and require zero rows for a flat sequence 100,100,100,100,100,100; a sequence whose only increase occurs at the 06:04 predecessor outside the target window; a decrease/reset 100,100,1,1,1,1; only three valid target deltas; gaps over 120 seconds; wrong object, counter, source type, host/instance mapping, or inactive inventory; nonnumeric, negative, or fractional counts; and a valid increase with an exact active host/adapter-ID/counter exception. An exception expiring exactly at dispatch or missing reason/ticket/owner must not suppress. Resets, wraps, missing/duplicate/late samples, unmapped instances, and counter disappearance must surface in companion health, never as zero loss.

dataSources: Native Windows Performance Monitor input on every in-scope Hyper-V host, sampled every 60 seconds with object `Network Interface`, exact counters `Packets Received Discarded`, `Packets Received Errors`, `Packets Outbound Discarded`, and `Packets Outbound Errors`, and inventoried instances. These are raw packet counts, so SPL computes adjacent-sample deltas rather than summing sampled Values. Local `index=perfmon` and `sourcetype=perfmon:Network_Interface` are deployment conventions. Required fields are `_time, _indextime, host, sourcetype, object, counter, instance, Value`. `hyperv_host_network_interface_inventory.csv` maps exact host/instance to stable adapter identity, role, and Hyper-V switch context; topology and exception data are deployment-owned.
app: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (Splunkbase 742) for supported Windows collection context plus a deployment-owned native perfmon input/search app. The add-on does not automatically prove this exact stanza or Hyper-V interface mapping. No Universal Forwarder Splunkbase app ID, generic `Perfmon:HyperV` source type, or undocumented Hyper-V dropped-packet counter is claimed.

index=perfmon sourcetype="perfmon:Network_Interface" object="Network Interface" counter IN ("Packets Received Discarded","Packets Received Errors","Packets Outbound Discarded","Packets Outbound Errors") earliest=-11m@m latest=@m
| eval sample_epoch=_time, packet_count=tonumber(Value)
| where packet_count>=0 AND packet_count=floor(packet_count)
| lookup hyperv_host_network_interface_inventory.csv host instance OUTPUT monitor_enabled adapter_id adapter_name adapter_role vm_switch_id vm_switch_name owner service_name runbook monitor_from_epoch monitor_until_epoch
| eval monitor_from_epoch=tonumber(monitor_from_epoch), monitor_until_epoch=tonumber(monitor_until_epoch), inventory_active=if(lower(trim(monitor_enabled))="true" AND len(adapter_id)>0 AND monitor_from_epoch<=now() AND monitor_until_epoch>now(),1,0)
| where inventory_active=1
| sort 0 host instance counter sample_epoch _indextime
| streamstats current=f window=1 last(packet_count) AS previous_count last(sample_epoch) AS previous_epoch by host instance counter
| eval sample_gap_seconds=sample_epoch-previous_epoch, reset_detected=if(isnotnull(previous_count) AND packet_count<previous_count,1,0), packet_delta=if(packet_count>=previous_count AND sample_gap_seconds>=30 AND sample_gap_seconds<=120,packet_count-previous_count,null()), target_start=relative_time(now(),"-5m@m"), target_end=relative_time(now(),"@m")

| eval finding=case(counter="Packets Received Discarded","received_discard_increase",counter="Packets Received Errors","received_error_increase",counter="Packets Outbound Discarded","outbound_discard_increase",counter="Packets Outbound Errors","outbound_error_increase"), severity=if(match(counter,"Errors$"),"high","medium")
| lookup hyperv_host_network_interface_exceptions.csv host adapter_id counter OUTPUT exception_until_epoch reason AS exception_reason ticket exception_owner
| eval exception_until_epoch=tonumber(exception_until_epoch), exception_active=if(exception_until_epoch>now() AND len(exception_reason)>0 AND len(ticket)>0 AND len(exception_owner)>0,1,0)

| eval unit="packets", threshold_packets=0, observation_semantics="adjacent_delta_of_windows_network_interface_raw_packet_count_not_hyperv_switch_port_loss_or_rate", use_case_id="UC-2.2.9"
| table target_start target_end host instance adapter_id adapter_name adapter_role vm_switch_id vm_switch_name counter finding severity packet_increment unit latest_raw_count sample_count distinct_sample_times valid_delta_count reset_detected threshold_packets owner service_name runbook last_indexed observation_semantics use_case_id

description: Runs every five minutes and evaluates the preceding closed five-minute window. For each governed Hyper-V host interface and documented discard/error counter, it computes valid adjacent deltas from 60-second raw packet counts and emits one row when at least four deltas are available, no reset occurred, and the total increase is greater than zero packets.
value: New interface discards or errors can precede degraded VM connectivity, cluster heartbeat loss, backup failure, or application timeouts. Correct raw-count differencing and governed adapter identity give network and virtualization teams a precise early signal while preserving the topology and sample evidence needed to distinguish buffer pressure, physical faults, host networking, virtual-switch policy, telemetry resets, and remote-path issues.
implementation: Deploy a native 60-second perfmon stanza for exact English `Network Interface` counter names with `useEnglishOnly=1`. Inventory each exact host/instance against a stable adapter ID, physical/vEthernet role, and `Get-VMSwitch` context; validate raw count units and names against Performance Monitor and `Get-NetAdapterStatistics`. Save the SPL every five minutes with an extra predecessor sample, require four valid 30–120-second deltas, reject reset buckets, and alert on any positive packet increase. Operate inventory-first sample/mapping health and diagnose physical, host, virtual-switch, guest, and service evidence before an approved network change.
visualization: Put telemetry trust first: expected-interface coverage, samples and valid deltas per window, duplicate times, 30–120-second gap compliance, reset/wrap buckets, invalid Values, source/object/counter drift, unmapped instances, inventory collisions, and indexing delay. Then show current packet increments by host, stable adapter ID, instance, role, virtual switch, counter, owner, and severity; a cumulative-count and derived-delta timeline; recurrence; and top interfaces/clusters. Drill down to `Get-NetAdapterStatistics`, Performance Monitor, physical NIC/switch telemetry, `Get-VMSwitch`, `Get-VMNetworkAdapter -All`, QoS/ACL/extension configuration, VMQ/RSS/vRSS/SR-IOV, packet capture, guest counters, and service probes. Do not label a host-interface row a VM or switch-port drop.
dataModelAcceleration: Not applicable. No accelerated CIM dataset is asserted to preserve exact Windows `Network Interface` raw packet counters, adjacent-sample delta/reset semantics, native instance, stable adapter mapping, virtual-switch context, and sample completeness. Raw perfmon events plus governed topology remain primary.

references.title: Microsoft Learn: Detecting bottlenecks in a virtualized environment

knownFalsePositives:
A row means an accepted Windows interface counter increased. It may reflect expected test traffic or a lower-impact path, but the increment itself is not fabricated.

1. **Approved failover, load, or packet-loss test** — Network or cluster engineers may deliberately create congestion or validate resilience. Confirm exact host/adapter ID, tool, source/destination, operator, change/test ID, expected counter/delta, service guardrails, start/end, and rollback. Use only an exact interface/counter exception for the bounded exercise.

2. **Planned NIC, virtual-switch, or driver maintenance** — Rebinding an external switch, changing a team, updating firmware/driver, or restarting an adapter can create errors and reset counters. Correlate Device Manager/NetAdapter state, `Get-VMSwitch`, cluster drain, change window, counter reset, and service probes. A reset is source health; post-change positive increments remain actionable.

3. **Known backup, migration, replication, or batch burst** — High traffic can expose receive-buffer or queue pressure and increment discard counters. Identify exact job/VM/path, throughput, VMQ/RSS/vRSS state, host CPU/DPC, physical switch queues, application impact, and completion. Expected workload does not make recurrent loss healthy.

4. **Management-OS vEthernet path rather than guest path** — A mapped `vEthernet` instance can report host management traffic and not a particular VM. Confirm adapter role, switch ID, management-OS adapter from `Get-VMNetworkAdapter -ManagementOS`, physical uplink, and affected endpoints. Route accurately; do not assign the row to a VM by name guess.

5. **Driver/firmware counter quirk or offload transition** — VMQ, RSS, RSC, SR-IOV, teaming, or vendor driver changes can alter where counters increment or reset. Compare driver/firmware versions, supported statistics, `Get-NetAdapterStatistics`, physical switch, packet capture, offload state, and a known traffic test. Document validated platform behavior rather than suppressing an entire vendor family.

6. **Duplicate collection or delayed samples** — Overlapping perfmon stanzas, two forwarders, clock skew, or indexing backfill can create duplicate times or invalid gaps. Compare `_cd`, source, forwarder, effective inputs, `_time`, `_indextime`, and raw sequence. The rule requires distinct current times and bounded gaps; companion health must drive correction.

7. **Counter reset or 32-bit wrap** — Reboot, adapter restart, interface recreation, or raw-counter wrap can produce a decrease. The primary blocks any reset bucket instead of converting it into packet loss. Verify uptime, adapter identity, driver events, and next samples; do not replace the decrease with zero silently.

**Suppression mechanism:** lookup hyperv_host_network_interface_exceptions.csv matches exact `host,adapter_id,counter` and requires future numeric expiry, reason, ticket, and owner. It applies only after a complete positive-delta window. Expired/malformed exceptions, resets/wraps, missing/duplicate/late samples, mapping drift, physical-switch errors, guest loss, and service impact remain visible in companion controls.

detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and corrected measurement claim

Assign Hyper-V, Failover Clustering, Windows networking, physical network, security/virtual-switch extension, capacity, workload, Splunk data/content, CMDB, and incident/change owners. Inventory every monitored interface by canonical Splunk host, exact perfmon instance, stable Windows adapter identity, interface alias/description/index/GUID as qualified, physical or management-OS `vEthernet` role, external switch ID/name, team/SET membership, speed, VLAN/QoS, owner, service, and lifecycle. Perfmon instance names are not immutable and can differ from friendly aliases.

The former UC claimed `Hyper-V Virtual Network Adapter\Dropped Packets Incoming/Outgoing` and generic `Perfmon:HyperV`. Primary Microsoft guidance documents `Hyper-V Virtual Network Adapter\Bytes/sec` for VM throughput, not those drop counters. Microsoft documents four potential-problem counters under `Network Interface(*)` and `Network Adapter(*)`: `Packets Received Discarded`, `Packets Received Errors`, `Packets Outbound Discarded`, and `Packets Outbound Errors`. This rewrite uses those exact host-interface counters and narrows the title accordingly.

Microsoft's WMI class marks these fields `PERF_COUNTER_RAWCOUNT`: the observed value is a packet count, not packets/sec. Discards are packets dropped without a detected delivery/transmission error; error counters represent packets discarded because of errors. Therefore summing sampled Values is wrong. The search subtracts adjacent values and sums positive deltas. Any increase above zero is local notification policy, not a universal Microsoft incident threshold.

This does not provide per-Hyper-V-switch-port attribution. `Get-VMSwitch` supplies switch identity and type; `Get-VMNetworkAdapter -All` supplies VM and management-OS virtual adapters for topology. SR-IOV and extensions can change packet paths. Use supported Windows/Hyper-V/NIC/forwarder combinations qualified locally; this review ran none and makes no `splunkVersions` assertion.

## Step 1 — Configure the exact native perfmon input

Deploy a version-controlled app with an input equivalent to:

```ini
[perfmon://HyperVHostNetworkInterface]
object = Network Interface
counters = Packets Received Discarded;Packets Received Errors;Packets Outbound Discarded;Packets Outbound Errors
instances = *
interval = 60
useEnglishOnly = 1
mode = single
index = perfmon
sourcetype = perfmon:Network_Interface
disabled = 0
```

Splunk requires one stanza per object and exact valid counter names. With `useEnglishOnly=1`, object/counter wildcard and regex matching are unavailable, while `instances=*` is supported. Index and source type are local. Validate the effective configuration and do not assume Splunkbase 742 creates this stanza.

On every Windows build/language/NIC cohort, use Performance Monitor > Add Counters or `typeperf -qx` to prove object, four counters, instance names, 60-second cadence, integer packet values, host, `_time`, and `_indextime`. Compare raw Splunk values with `Get-NetAdapterStatistics`, whose Microsoft-documented statistics include discards and errors. Record whether a driver supports each statistic; unsupported/stuck fields are health findings, not zeros.

Create `hyperv_host_network_interface_inventory.csv` with unique `host,instance,monitor_enabled,adapter_id,adapter_name,adapter_role,vm_switch_id,vm_switch_name,owner,service_name,runbook,monitor_from_epoch,monitor_until_epoch`. Generate/reconcile it from `Get-NetAdapter`, `Get-VMSwitch`, `Get-VMNetworkAdapter -ManagementOS/-All`, and CMDB topology. Create `hyperv_host_network_interface_exceptions.csv` keyed by exact `host,adapter_id,counter` with expiry/reason/ticket/owner. Reject wildcard, duplicate, ambiguous, and indefinite records.

## Step 2 — Establish sample, reset, and mapping health

Build an inventory-first companion search for absent interfaces, fewer than expected samples, duplicate `_time`, gaps outside 30–120 seconds, invalid/fractional/negative Values, future/late time, counter/object/source-type drift, one instance mapped to multiple adapter IDs, one adapter reported under multiple active instances, unmapped observations, inactive observations, and indexing delay. Track each counter separately because driver support can differ.

A raw count can decrease after host reboot, adapter restart/recreation, driver reset, or 32-bit wrap. Report every decrease with host uptime and adapter events. The primary blocks a whole host/instance/counter window when any reset appears; it never uses `abs`, clamps the decrease, or treats it as packet loss. After identity changes, require a new baseline predecessor before calculating deltas.

Duplicate collection can make two events share one timestamp but different Values. Do not choose arbitrarily. Reconcile effective app precedence, source/forwarder, `_cd`, and input assignment. Missing samples are unknown; never fill them with the prior count or zero merely to satisfy four deltas.

## Step 3 — Save and understand the adjacent-delta SPL

Save the supplied SPL as `hyperv_host_interface_discard_or_error_increase` and run every five minutes after the closed boundary is expected to index. `earliest=-11m@m latest=@m` supplies enough history for each current sample's predecessor. The rule filters exact object/counters and valid packet counts, joins active exact inventory, and sorts ascending by host, instance, counter, event time, and index time.

`streamstats current=f window=1` carries only the preceding sample. A delta is valid when current count is not lower and the gap is 30–120 seconds. The search then keeps only samples in the preceding aligned five-minute target. At least four current sample times and four valid deltas are required; any reset blocks the window; `sum(packet_delta)>0` is measured packets newly added to that raw counter during accepted intervals.

The row grain is one host/instance/counter/window. Error counters route high and discard counters medium by local policy; packet increment is not Microsoft severity. Alert by stable adapter ID/counter and update the same incident across adjacent windows, retaining each result. Include raw series, topology, source-health, change window, and service probes. Apply exceptions only after the complete finding.

## Step 4 — Validate counts, deltas, and boundaries

Run the fixed positive sequence and independently calculate deltas 0,1,0,3,0 for a total of four packets. Assert one row, five current samples/deltas, and preserved adapter/switch identity. Run every negative independently. Add tests for an increase at the predecessor boundary, increase at target start/end, constant values, multiple increases, counter at 0, large 32-bit values, fractional/text/null/negative values, reset/wrap, reboot, 29/30/120/121-second gaps, duplicate timestamps, out-of-order indexing, instance rename, inventory activation/expiry equality, and exception expiry equality.

On a nonproduction Hyper-V host, compare six consecutive Performance Monitor and raw Splunk readings with `Get-NetAdapterStatistics`. Use an existing approved traffic or loss test; do not disable interfaces or flood production to create evidence. Confirm each packet increment and distinguish receive/outbound discard/error. Verify alert, throttle, dashboard, lookup replication, search-peer failure, and recovery after a zero-increment window.

Test host reboot, NIC restart, driver update, external-switch rebinding, SET/team change, live migration, VMQ/RSS/vRSS/SR-IOV change, virtual adapter add/remove, and forwarder restart. Every case must yield correct primary behavior or explicit health status. Keep `status=draft` until virtualization, network, workload, and Splunk owners accept versions, counter support/type, mapping, fixtures, source health, routing, and response.

## Step 5 — Diagnose the packet path before changing it

Responder sequence: (1) verify raw counts, predecessor, deltas, sample gaps, no reset, stable adapter ID, and current Performance Monitor/`Get-NetAdapterStatistics`; (2) determine whether the instance is a physical uplink, team/SET member, or management-OS vEthernet adapter; (3) map external switch and virtual adapters with `Get-VMSwitch` and `Get-VMNetworkAdapter -All`; (4) compare physical switch port errors/discards, speed/duplex, optics/cable, queues/buffers, MTU/VLAN, and NIC driver/firmware; (5) inspect VMQ, RSS/vRSS, RSC, SR-IOV, QoS, ACL, extension/filter, Windows Filtering Platform, and host CPU/DPC/interrupt pressure; (6) compare guest adapter counters, packet capture at supported points, source/destination/remote path, and service probes; (7) correlate migration, backup, replication, load, patch, or network change; (8) approve the least risky correction with rollback; and (9) verify no new increments plus end-to-end service health.

Do not automatically disable/enable an adapter, rebind a VMSwitch, change VLAN/MTU/QoS/ACL, alter VMQ/RSS/vRSS/RSC/SR-IOV, update driver/firmware, migrate a VM, restart a host, or remove an extension. Those changes can disconnect management, cluster, storage, or tenant traffic. Require out-of-band access, redundancy/quorum, vendor support, maintenance, rollback, and workload validation.

A positive host-interface delta does not establish root cause. Receive discards can reflect buffer pressure; errors can indicate hardware/link/driver problems; switch policies/extensions can intentionally drop; remote devices can cause symptoms without this counter; and a guest may be affected while host counters stay flat. Continue packet-path diagnosis and preserve uncertainty.

## Step 6 — Troubleshoot detector failures

- **Object/counter absent:** verify exact names with Performance Monitor/typeperf, Windows build, NIC/driver support, `useEnglishOnly=1`, Hyper-V host role, and splunkd perfmon errors.
- **Value stays nonzero but no alert:** expected when the cumulative raw count is flat. The rule detects new packets, not historical total.
- **Value rises but no alert:** inspect predecessor range, sample gaps, reset flag, inventory, active times, source type, and dispatch boundary.
- **Counter falls:** treat as reset/wrap/identity change; inspect uptime, adapter and driver events, mapping, and next baseline.
- **Instance vanished after switch/team change:** rebuild governed mapping from stable adapter/topology identity; do not wildcard-match a similar name.
- **Physical switch shows loss but Windows does not:** the loss may be outside the measured interface statistic or unsupported/offloaded. Continue device and packet-path evidence.
- **Guest reports loss but host interface is flat:** inspect guest vNIC/OS, Hyper-V switch policies/extensions, SR-IOV path, remote network, and application behavior.
- **Duplicates create conflicting counts:** stop primary interpretation for that key, repair input ownership, and retain both raw records for evidence.
grandmaExplanation: We watch the Hyper-V host's network-card counters and compare each reading with the one before it. If new packets were discarded or damaged, the network team investigates the exact adapter and path instead of blaming a virtual machine automatically.
